title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll dealt the Mérida sign-painter's wall. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Pride in the students, never playful, never a folk postcard.

options.label: Rótulo de Mérida
options.lineage: Hand-painted shop signs (rótulos) on Mérida's lime-washed walls
options.thesis: The campaign is painted on the wall like a neighborhood announcement: big, proud, impossible to miss.
materials: sign-painter caps with a flat painted shadow
options.viewport: An Izamal-yellow wall with 'MÉRIDA VA A MEXICO DREAMIN'' lettered in blue with a flat shadow, an añil band with the amount raised and the remaining gap, amount tiles and a black donate sign within reach of the thumb.
options.risk: It drifts toward folk or playful if the lettering gets decorative; it only works if it's lettered with sign-trade discipline: flat, straight and big.

raised.raise: The amount still missing is painted as boldly as the amount raised: 'FALTAN $18,750'.
The newest supporter is painted darkest, and older names fade like weathered paint.
The students' story sits in one calm column, a clearing in the wall.
Depth comes only from overlapping flat coats of paint: no gradients, no blur.
Almagre red is reserved for the one element in motion: the chosen amount, the active step.

options.label: Boleto Mérida → CDMX
options.lineage: Long-distance bus tickets and boarding passes
options.thesis: The campaign is the trip ticket: each donation moves the students along the 1,320 km from Mérida to Mexico City.
options.viewport: A ticket on a deep teal background: MID → CDMX with the route line advancing, the headline, and a perforated stub with amounts and the donate button.
options.risk: The travel ticket is a familiar metaphor, and many runs land there; it's clear but less memorable.

options.label: Three-ink kiosk
options.lineage: Printed goods from a kiosk, three inks on gray board
options.thesis: The whole site printed in three inks on recycled board: each amount is a cell, as at a stall.
options.viewport: A grid of whole cells: an abstract mark and headline, progress cell by cell, four amount cells and a black donate cell.
options.case: Wins on clarity (amounts as cells, progress in segments), but relatives and companies don't recognize themselves in a Central European kiosk.
options.risk: Cold and austere; it can read like a design exercise and not like students from Mérida.

options.label: Seven-segment scoreboard
options.thesis: Progress as a scoreboard that jumps from 98 to 100.
options.viewport: A scoreboard with the amount raised in red segments.
options.case: The dark tech look clashes with 'serious and close'; little identification.
options.kept: The missing amount is drawn as deliberately as the raised amount.

options.label: Suminagashi ink
options.thesis: A basin of ink that answers the finger.
options.case: No relation to the students or to donating; heavy on phones.
options.kept: The newest is the darkest: the most recent supporter stands out.

options.label: Secession border
options.thesis: A floral border that grows toward the text.
options.viewport: Text in a clearing of flowers.
options.case: Ornamental, and close to folk; it doesn't help donating.
options.kept: The story in one calm column.

options.label: Layered papercut
options.thesis: Depth from layers of flat paper.
options.case: It turns into papel picado: exactly the folk postcard you ruled out.
options.kept: Depth by overlapping flat coats, never by shading.

options.label: Paper automata
options.thesis: A procession of paper figures moved by a crank.
options.case: Too playful for companies and evaluators.
options.kept: One reserved color only for what's moving.

canonCard.label: The crowdfunding standard
canonCard.thesis: The GoFundMe-style campaign page done with care: photo, progress, donate button.
canonCard.viewport: Large photo, title, progress bar, a round donate button, and the supporters.
canonCard.risk: Exactly the generic charity look you said would feel wrong.
